blocks.title: The big idea
blocks.body: An agent combines a model, application-controlled tools, an observation-and-action loop and state. Use the simplest design that meets the goal. Tool use and coordination do not guarantee correct results.

blocks.title: Choose the control level
items: Direct edit: a small, clear change
Workflow: predefined paths for a known sequence
One agent: bounded decisions for an uncertain path
Parallel agents: independent slices with explicit contracts

blocks.title: Tool and permission rules
items: The model requests; application code executes or denies
Use narrow tools with typed inputs and clear outputs
Validate values, paths and state before acting
Grant least privilege and sandbox the working area
Require human approval for destructive or external actions

blocks.title: Coordinate independent work
items: Define objectives, interfaces, outputs and done evidence
Assign one writer per file or separate working areas
Let builders produce and reviewers inspect
Give shared integration files to the orchestrator
Sequence work when decisions remain tightly dependent

blocks.title: Experimental shared artifacts
items: Task records: decisions, artifacts, checks and open questions
Negative results: failed approaches with useful evidence
Optional commit DAG: parent lineage for related attempts
Lineage and notes do not prove correctness or compatibility

blocks.title: Evaluate the whole system
items: Outcomes: inspect real environment changes
Traces: inspect requests, decisions, results and errors
Cases: cover typical, boundary and adversarial behavior
Integration: rerun the full relevant suite
Trials: repeat variable runs and preserve failures

blocks.body: Finish the capstone with a human release or hold decision based on outcomes, checks, traces, permissions and remaining risks. Agent self-reports are not release evidence.
